description: A resonant filter with a one pole stage, a two pole stage and a ring modulation between their low and high pass halves

params.text: Sets the corner of the two pole filter, four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets how far the MOD input moves the two pole corner, -2 to 2 octaves per volt
Sets the resonance of the two pole filter, -6dB at fully counter-clockwise to 30dB fully clockwise
Sets the corner of the one pole stages, four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets how far the MOD input moves the one pole corner, -2 to 2 octaves per volt
Sets the level of the ring modulation added to the main output, silent at fully counter-clockwise and one and a half times fully clockwise

inputs.text: A signal into both the one pole low pass and the one pole high pass
Moves both filter corners together, one octave per volt
A signal added into the one pole low pass after a four sample estimate of where it is going next
A signal added after the one pole stage, straight into the two pole filter and so past the ring modulation
Moves the two filter corners by the amounts the MOD and MAM knobs set
A signal added to the first input before the one pole high pass

outputs.text: The one pole low pass output
The two pole filter output with the ring modulation added, which is the module's main output
The two pole corner frequency, sent out as one volt for every hertz, so it reaches thousands of volts at ordinary settings
The one pole high pass output
The first input with the main output subtracted from it
The ring modulation on its own: the one pole low pass times the one pole high pass times the AM knob

notes: every input reads polyphonically and the outputs take the channel count of the widest input patched
the maker's own advice for hearing all six knobs at once is to patch into IN1, take LP12 out and use CV for tracking; the other jacks join the chain before or after some of the controls
